activities.description: Fly into Ngurah Rai airport and transfer to Ubud (about 90 minutes). Check into your guesthouse along Jalan Bisma.
Walk the Campuhan Ridge Walk at golden hour — a breezy trail above lush river valleys with zero crowds midweek.
Dinner at Locavore To Go for affordable tasting-menu-quality Indonesian dishes, then stroll Ubud's Royal Palace grounds.
Hire a scooter and ride to Tegallalang Rice Terraces early (arrive by 8 AM to beat tour buses). Walk the lower paths for the best photos.
Visit Tirta Empul water temple for a traditional purification ritual — bring a sarong and a respectful attitude.
Catch the Kecak fire dance at Uluwatu Temple at sunset — book front-row seats and watch for cheeky monkeys.
Drive north to Tibumana Waterfall — less touristy than Tegenungan, with a calm swimming pool at the base.
Continue to Kanto Lampo Waterfall for dramatic photos under the cascading rock face, then stop at Tukad Cepung, a hidden canyon waterfall.
Back in Ubud, take a Balinese cooking class at Paon Bali — learn to make lawar, sate lilit, and black rice pudding from a local family.
Transfer to Seminyak. Grab brunch at Sisterfields (their ricotta hotcakes are legendary) and settle into a beach hotel.
Rent a surfboard at Batu Bolong Beach in Canggu, or lounge at La Brisa beach club with a fresh coconut and ocean views.
Sunset drinks at Potato Head Beach Club, then wander to Sarong for refined Indonesian fine dining.
Book a 2-hour Balinese massage and flower bath at Spa Alila or a local Jimbaran spa — the perfect finale.
Visit the fish market at Jimbaran Bay, pick your catch, and have it grilled beachside at one of the seafood warungs.
Last sunset on Jimbaran Beach before your transfer to the airport. Grab last-minute Balinese coffee beans as souvenirs.
Start at the Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew (Temple of the Emerald Buddha). Arrive right at 8:30 AM opening to beat the heat and crowds.
Walk to Wat Pho for the massive reclining Buddha, then get a traditional Thai massage at the temple's own massage school.
Cross the river by ferry to Wat Arun and watch it glow at sunset, then eat pad thai at Thipsamai on Maha Chai Road.
Take the BTS to Chatuchak Weekend Market (or JJ Green on weekdays) — over 15,000 stalls of everything imaginable.
Cool off at the nearby Chatuchak Park, then head to Or Tor Kor Market for the best tropical fruit you'll ever taste.
Join a Chinatown street food walk along Yaowarat Road — must-tries include Nai Ek's rolled noodles and mango sticky rice from Mae Varee.
Hire a longtail boat through the Thonburi canals (khlongs) — see stilted houses, a floating market, and the daily life most tourists miss.
Explore the Jim Thompson House, a gorgeous teak museum surrounded by gardens, then browse the boutiques of Siam Square.
Sunset cocktails at Vertigo Rooftop Bar on the 61st floor of the Banyan Tree, then dinner at Somtum Der for Isaan cuisine.
Early drive to Damnoen Saduak Floating Market (leave by 7 AM). Paddle through vendors selling grilled skewers and coconut pancakes.
Stop at the Maeklong Railway Market on the way back — watch vendors fold their stalls as a train passes inches away.
Back in Bangkok, explore Asiatique the Riverfront night market and catch a Muay Thai show at Rajadamnern Stadium.
Visit Wat Saket (Golden Mount) and climb the 300 steps for a panoramic view of old Bangkok without the crowds.
Explore the ICONSIAM mega-mall's basement floor — a recreation of a Thai floating market indoors with incredible food stalls.
Final meal at Jay Fai, the legendary Michelin-starred street food chef — get the crab omelet. Book ahead or arrive early.
Explore Wat Chedi Luang and Wat Phra Singh inside the moated Old City — these 14th-century temples are walking distance apart.
Join a half-day Thai cooking class at Mama Noi's or Cookery Magic — you'll shop at a local market and cook five dishes.
Walk the Sunday Night Market on Ratchadamnoen Road for handmade crafts, sausages, and mango sticky rice.
Drive or songthaew up to Wat Phra That Doi Suthep — climb 306 steps flanked by naga serpents for gold-spired temple views over the city.
Continue to the Hmong hill tribe village of Doi Pui for handwoven textiles and mountain coffee with stunning valley views.
Back in town, eat at SP Chicken (the best rotisserie chicken in Thailand — just ask anyone) and explore Nimmanhaemin Road's cafes.
Visit Elephant Nature Park (book ahead!) — an ethical rescue sanctuary where you feed, walk with, and bathe elephants. No riding.
Continue at the sanctuary learning about rescue stories, or head to Bua Tong Sticky Waterfalls where you can climb UP the limestone cascade.
Khao soi dinner at Khao Soi Khun Yai — this Northern Thai coconut curry noodle dish is the region's signature and this shop is the gold standard.
Explore Baan Kang Wat, an artist village of wooden houses turned into studios, galleries, and craft coffee shops.
Visit the stunning white Wat Rong Khun (White Temple) if you have time for a 3-hour roundtrip to Chiang Rai, or explore MAIIAM Contemporary Art Museum.
Final stroll through the Chiang Mai Night Bazaar for last souvenirs, then farewell dinner at Huen Phen for royal Northern Thai cuisine.
Dive straight into the Old Quarter's 36 streets. Start at Dong Xuan Market, then wind through Hang Bac (silver street) and Hang Gai (silk street).
Walk around Hoan Kiem Lake to Ngoc Son Temple on the tiny island. Grab an egg coffee at Giang Cafe — the original since 1946.
Pull up a tiny plastic stool on a busy corner and eat bun cha at Bun Cha Huong Lien (where Obama ate). Finish with bia hoi on Ta Hien Beer Street.
Visit the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex, including his stilt house and the One Pillar Pagoda — arrive before 10 AM as lines grow fast.
Explore the Temple of Literature, Vietnam's first university from 1070 AD, then visit the excellent Vietnamese Women's Museum nearby.
Attend a water puppet show at Thang Long Theatre — a uniquely Vietnamese art form — then dinner at Cha Ca La Vong for the iconic turmeric fish dish.

days.title: Day Trip to Ha Long Bay

activities.description: Depart early for Ha Long Bay (4-hour drive or 2-hour shuttle to port). Board a traditional junk boat and cruise past thousands of limestone karsts.
Kayak through Luon Cave into a hidden lagoon, swim from the boat, and feast on a fresh seafood lunch cooked onboard.
Watch the sunset from the top deck as the boat anchors in the bay, or if doing a day trip, enjoy the scenic drive back to Hanoi.
Walk the Long Bien Bridge, then explore the chaotic Long Bien Market below where local vendors sell produce at dawn.
Take a guided street food tour through the Old Quarter — try pho bo at Pho Thin, banh mi at Banh Mi 25, and bun bo nam bo at a hidden alley spot.
Cross to the West Lake area for sunset drinks at a lakeside cafe, then dinner at Bun Cha Ta in the French Quarter.
Visit Hanoi's famous Train Street (check current access — cafes nearby offer views) and the nearby Hoa Lo Prison museum (the Hanoi Hilton).
Shop for lacquerware and silk at craft shops in Hang Gai Street, then relax with a Vietnamese coffee at Cong Caphe in the Old Quarter.
Final pho at Pho Gia Truyen on Bat Dan Street (the city's most beloved bowl) before heading to Noi Bai International Airport.
Wake before dawn to witness the alms giving ceremony — hundreds of saffron-robed monks walk silently collecting sticky rice from kneeling locals.
Climb 328 steps to the top of Mount Phousi for a 360-degree view of the town, the Mekong, and the Nam Khan rivers merging below.
Browse the Luang Prabang Night Market for handwoven textiles and hill tribe crafts, then eat at Tamarind restaurant for authentic Lao tasting plates.
Drive 30 minutes to Kuang Si Falls — arrive early to have the turquoise pools almost to yourself. Visit the bear rescue center at the entrance.
Swim in the lower pools, hike the trail to the top of the main falls, and picnic on the wooden platforms surrounded by jungle.
Back in town, try Lao BBQ (sin dat) at a riverside restaurant — you grill your own meats and dip vegetables in a bubbling broth ring.
Board a slow boat upriver to the Pak Ou Caves — two limestone caverns stuffed with thousands of gold Buddha statues left by pilgrims.
Stop at a riverside Lao Lao whisky village to taste rice wine, then cruise back watching water buffalo graze along the Mekong banks.
Walk through Wat Xieng Thong, the most stunning temple in Laos, as late afternoon light hits the golden mosaics.
Visit the morning market at the tip of the peninsula — locals sell river weed, fresh fish, and herbs. Try khao piak sen (Lao noodle soup) for breakfast.
Tour the Royal Palace Museum (Haw Kham) to see Lao royal artifacts and the Phra Bang — the sacred golden Buddha the city is named for.
Farewell sunset from a Mekong-side bar like Utopia (lounge on cushions overlooking the Nam Khan River), then head to the airport.
Fly into El Nido via Lio Airport and settle into your beachfront cottage in Corong Corong or the town proper.
Walk along Las Cabanas Beach — rent a kayak or just swim in the calm cove framed by limestone cliffs.
Watch the sunset from the Las Cabanas zipline viewpoint deck, then eat grilled seafood at Trattoria Altrove for surprisingly great Italian-Filipino fusion.
Board an outrigger bangka for Tour A — first stop is the Big Lagoon, paddling through towering karst walls into impossibly clear emerald water.
Swim and snorkel at Small Lagoon (rent a kayak inside), then visit Shimizu Island for coral reefs teeming with tropical fish.
Return to town for a beachside dinner at Happiness Beach Bar. Order the kinilaw (Filipino ceviche) and an ice-cold San Miguel.
Tour C takes you further out — start with the Hidden Beach, a tiny strip of sand only accessible by swimming through a narrow gap in the rocks.
Snorkel at Matinloc Shrine and swim through the crystal-clear waters of Star Beach, a remote sandbar with almost no one around.
Back in town, try a boodle fight dinner (communal Filipino feast on banana leaves) at El Nido Boutique & Artcafe.
Rent a motorbike and ride 45 minutes to Nacpan Beach — a 4-kilometer golden sand stretch that's one of the most beautiful in the Philippines.
Lounge under a palm tree, swim in gentle waves, and grab grilled fish and mango shakes from the simple beachfront shacks.
Ride back through coconut palm roads, then climb to the Taraw Cliff viewpoint (steep but short) for a sunset panorama over the entire bay.
Rent a private kayak and paddle to Cadlao Island — the massive limestone island right across from town has secret beaches and coves.
Last swim at the town beach, shop for woven bags and coconut bowls at the local market, and pack up.
Farewell seafood feast at Maremegmeg Beach with sunset views before heading to the airport for your evening flight.
Wake at 4:30 AM and ride a tuk-tuk to Angkor Wat for sunrise. Position yourself at the left reflecting pool for the iconic silhouette shot.
Explore the Angkor Wat complex in detail — the bas-reliefs on the south gallery depicting the Churning of the Sea of Milk are jaw-dropping.
Cool down with a craft beer at Miss Wong cocktail bar, then dinner at Cuisine Wat Damnak — a Cambodian fine-dining gem using local ingredients.
Start at Bayon Temple in Angkor Thom — 216 massive stone faces smile down at you from every direction. Arrive before 8 AM for misty photos.
Walk to Ta Prohm, the jungle temple where massive silk-cotton trees swallow the ruins (the Tomb Raider temple). Then visit the quieter Preah Khan.
Phare, the Cambodian Circus — a must-see show combining acrobatics, music, and stories of Cambodian history. Book tickets ahead.
Ride a bicycle to the smaller temple of Banteay Srei (30 km out) — its pink sandstone carvings are the finest in all of Angkor.
Visit the Landmine Museum to learn about Cambodia's history and the heroic work of Aki Ra, then cool off at a local swimming pool.
Explore Pub Street and the night market, but eat at Genevieve's for elevated Khmer cuisine away from the tourist crush.
Take a boat to the Kompong Khleang floating village on Tonle Sap Lake — far more authentic than Kompong Phluk with stilted houses towering above the water.
Visit Artisans Angkor workshop to see young Cambodians learning traditional silk weaving and stone carving — great for meaningful souvenirs.
Final amok fish (Cambodian coconut curry steamed in banana leaf) at Haven Training Restaurant, which supports at-risk youth.
Start at Meiji Shrine surrounded by an ancient forest in the middle of the city. Walk the gravel path under towering torii gates.
Explore Harajuku's Takeshita Street for wild fashion, then walk to Omotesando for architect-designed flagship stores and quiet cat cafes.
Cross the Shibuya Scramble at peak hour, then head to Nonbei Yokocho (Drunkard's Alley) — six tiny bars in a row, each seating four people.
Hit Tsukiji Outer Market by 7 AM for the freshest sushi breakfast of your life. Try tamagoyaki (sweet egg) and fresh uni at the street stalls.
Walk through upscale Ginza for department store food halls (depachika) — the basement of Mitsukoshi has the best free samples in Tokyo.
Explore Akihabara's neon-lit electronics shops and multi-floor arcades, then eat ramen at Fuunji in Shinjuku — expect a line but it moves fast.
Visit Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa — Tokyo's oldest temple. Walk through the Kaminarimon thunder gate and browse Nakamise shopping street.
Cross the Sumida River to Tokyo Skytree for 360-degree views, then explore the Yanaka neighborhood — old Tokyo with temple cats and traditional shops.
Dinner in Asakusa at Sometaro, a DIY okonomiyaki place in a beautiful old wooden house, then stroll the lantern-lit streets.
Take the JR line to Kamakura (1 hour). Start at Kotoku-in Temple to see the Great Buddha — a 13-meter bronze statue sitting in the open since 1498.
Hike the Daibutsu trail through bamboo forests to Zeniarai Benten Shrine, where locals wash money in spring water for good luck.
Back in Tokyo, experience Golden Gai in Shinjuku — 200 tiny bars packed into six narrow alleys, each with its own personality.
Visit teamLab Borderless (now in Azabudai Hills) — an immersive digital art museum that redefines what art can be. Book timed entry online.
Explore Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden — cherry blossoms in spring, autumn foliage in fall, and peaceful green space any time of year.
Last meal at a yakitori alley under the Shinjuku train tracks (Omoide Yokocho), grilling chicken skewers with salaryman and travelers side by side.
Walk the Philosopher's Path from Ginkaku-ji (Silver Pavilion) south through cherry-tree-lined canals to Nanzen-ji Temple's massive gate.
Continue to the Eikan-do Temple, then Nanzen-ji's Roman-style brick aqueduct — an unexpected sight in the middle of ancient Kyoto.
Dinner in the Gion district — walk Hanamikoji Street looking for geiko (Kyoto geisha), then eat at Gion Kappa for approachable kaiseki cuisine.
Arrive at Fushimi Inari-taisha by 6:30 AM — hike through 10,000 vermillion torii gates up the mountain with barely anyone around.
Walk 10 minutes to the Fushimi sake district. Tour Gekkeikan Okura Sake Museum and taste premium sakes straight from the brewery.
Take the train to Pontocho Alley — a narrow lantern-lit lane of restaurants along the Kamogawa River. Grab a riverside seat for dinner.
Enter the Arashiyama Bamboo Grove at sunrise (before 7 AM) when the towering stalks creak in silence. Walk to the Okochi Sanso villa gardens.
Cross the Togetsukyo Bridge, then visit the Monkey Park Iwatayama — climb 15 minutes to feed wild macaques with panoramic valley views.
Ride the scenic Sagano Romantic Train back, then dinner at Shoraian — a tofu restaurant on a tiny island in the Oi River.
Visit Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion) — the gold-leaf temple reflected in its mirror pond is genuinely breathtaking even with crowds.
Walk through Nishiki Market (Kyoto's Kitchen) — sample pickled vegetables, mochi, fresh yuba (tofu skin), and matcha everything.
Experience a traditional tea ceremony at Camellia near Kenninji Temple, then explore the Higashiyama district's lantern-lit streets at night.
Tour Tofuku-ji Temple — its moss garden and autumn maples are legendary. Less visited than the big names but equally stunning.
Take a matcha-making workshop in Uji (20 minutes by train) — Japan's premier tea region. Visit Byodo-in Temple, the one on the 10-yen coin.
Final meal of Kyoto-style obanzai (home-style multi-dish dinner) at Aonisai, then one last walk through Gion at dusk.
Rent a hanbok (traditional dress) near Gyeongbokgung Palace — wearing one gets you free admission. Watch the changing of the guard at 10 AM.
Walk through Bukchon Hanok Village's narrow lanes of 600-year-old traditional houses, then browse Insadong's galleries and tea houses.
Dinner at Tosokchon Samgyetang near the palace for ginseng chicken soup, then stroll the Cheonggyecheon Stream lit up at night.
Explore Gwangjang Market — Korea's oldest and best market. Must-tries: bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap, and yukhoe (beef tartare).
Walk to Myeongdong for K-beauty shopping (sheet masks for everyone), then climb Namsan Tower for panoramic city views and love lock fences.
Korean BBQ at Mapo Galmaegi in Mapo-gu — pork galbi grilled over charcoal with soju and all the side dishes you can handle.
Join a guided DMZ tour (book 3+ days ahead, bring your passport). Stand in the Joint Security Area where soldiers from both Koreas face off meters apart.
Visit the Third Tunnel of Aggression and the Dora Observatory, where you can see into North Korea through binoculars.
Back in Seoul, decompress at a jjimjilbang (Korean spa) — Dragon Hill Spa in Yongsan has saunas, pools, and you can even sleep there.
Explore Ikseon-dong, a hanok neighborhood turned into Seoul's coolest cafe and boutique district. Get a croffle at one of the tiny pastry shops.
Cross the river to Gangnam and visit the COEX Starfield Library (the Instagram-famous bookshelf atrium), then explore Garosugil's tree-lined boutiques.
Fried chicken and beer (chimaek) at BHC Chicken, then experience Seoul's nightlife in Hongdae — live busking, dance clubs, and pojangmacha tent bars.
Hike Bukhansan National Park (Bukhansanseong trail) — granite peaks with city views, only 40 minutes from downtown by subway.
Visit Jogyesa Temple for a peaceful break, then last-minute shopping at Namdaemun Market for dried seaweed, ginseng, and Korean snacks.
Final bibimbap at Jeonju Jungang Hoegwan, then grab hotteok (sweet pancakes) from a street vendor before heading to Incheon Airport.
Take the Peak Tram up to Victoria Peak for the iconic harbor panorama. Walk the circular trail around the peak for quieter viewpoints.
Ride the world's longest escalator system down through SoHo and Sheung Wan, stopping at antique shops and street art along Hollywood Road.
Dim sum dinner at Tim Ho Wan (the world's cheapest Michelin star) in Sham Shui Po — the baked BBQ pork buns are legendary.
Take the Star Ferry across Victoria Harbour (the best 30 cents you'll spend), then explore the Tsim Sha Tsui waterfront promenade.
Dive into the madness of Mong Kok — Ladies' Market, Sneaker Street, and Goldfish Market, then eat egg waffles from a street cart.
Temple Street Night Market for fortune tellers and cheap eats, then rooftop drinks at Ozone Bar on the 118th floor of the ICC tower.
Ferry to Lantau Island. Ride the Ngong Ping 360 cable car for stunning views, then visit the Tian Tan Big Buddha and Po Lin Monastery.
Explore Tai O fishing village — stilt houses over the water, sun-dried seafood, and pink dolphins if you're lucky on a boat tour.
Back on Hong Kong Island, eat at Yat Lok for Michelin-starred roast goose — just point and sit. One of the best meals in the city for under $10.
Breakfast at Australia Dairy Company in Jordan — scrambled eggs and toast in the fastest, most chaotic service you'll ever experience.
Explore the PMQ creative hub in Central for local designer shops, then walk to Man Mo Temple — incense coils hanging from the ceiling since 1847.
Watch the Symphony of Lights show from Tsim Sha Tsui at 8 PM, then farewell dinner at Mak's Noodle for the city's finest wonton noodle soup.
Enter the Forbidden City through the Meridian Gate (book tickets online, they sell out). Spend 3 hours walking through 980 ancient buildings.
Exit north into Jingshan Park and climb the hill for a panoramic view looking back over the entire Forbidden City complex.
Explore Wangfujing Night Market for scorpion-on-a-stick photos, but eat real Beijing food at Da Dong for the city's best Peking duck.
Skip Badaling. Go to Mutianyu section instead (90 minutes from the city) — fewer crowds, more dramatic scenery, and a fun toboggan ride down.
Hike 2-3 hours along the wall's watchtowers, each offering increasingly spectacular views of the wall snaking over mountain ridges.
Back in Beijing, eat hand-pulled noodles at Zhang Mama near Nanluoguxiang — watch them stretch the dough before your eyes.
Take a rickshaw tour through the narrow hutong alleys around Shichahai Lake — these centuries-old neighborhoods are disappearing fast.
Visit the Lama Temple (Yonghegong), Beijing's most spectacular Buddhist temple, with a 26-meter Buddha carved from a single piece of sandalwood.
Bar-hop along the Houhai Lake bars, then dinner at Baijia Dayuan in a restored Qing Dynasty courtyard for traditional imperial cuisine.
Arrive at Temple of Heaven Park by 7 AM to see locals doing tai chi, playing erhu, and waltzing. The Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests is China's most iconic building.
Explore 798 Art District — a former weapons factory turned into Beijing's contemporary art hub with galleries, cafes, and murals.
Catch a Peking Opera show at Liyuan Theatre, then eat Sichuan hotpot at Haidilao — the service alone is worth the visit.
Spend the morning at the Summer Palace — take a dragon boat across Kunming Lake, walk the 728-meter Long Corridor painted with 14,000 scenes.
Visit the Olympic Park to see the Bird's Nest and Water Cube, then browse Panjiayuan Antique Market for Mao-era memorabilia and jade.
Final meal of jiaozi (dumplings) at Xian Lao Man — pork and chive is the classic — before heading to Beijing Capital Airport.
Start at Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall for the hourly changing of the guard ceremony, then walk through the Liberty Square gardens.
Ride the world's fastest elevator to the top of Taipei 101 for 360-degree views, then explore the luxury mall and Din Tai Fung in the basement.
Shilin Night Market — Taiwan's largest. Must-eats: stinky tofu, pepper buns, oyster omelets, and XXL fried chicken cutlets.
Bus to Jiufen Old Street (90 minutes) — the hilltop mining town that inspired Spirited Away. Arrive early before the crowds fill the alleys.
Sip taro ball soup at the famous Ah Gan Yi teahouse overlooking the Pacific, then explore the lantern-lit tunnels and tea shops.
Back in Taipei, eat beef noodle soup at Lin Dong Fang — arguably the best bowl in the city. Then walk the Ximending pedestrian area.
Visit Longshan Temple in Wanhua, Taipei's oldest and most active temple — watch locals burn incense and shake fortune sticks.
Walk to Dadaocheng and the Dihua Street fabric and tea district. Stop at ASW Tea House for oolong with a rooftop view.
Raohe Street Night Market for black pepper buns (the line is worth it) and stinky tofu, then walk the rainbow bridge along Keelung River.
Take the MRT to Beitou for a morning soak in natural hot springs — Millennium Hot Spring is public and only $2, or go to Villa 32 for luxury.
Hike Elephant Mountain (Xiangshan) for the best Taipei 101 photo op — a short steep climb with incredible views, especially at golden hour.
Final meal at Addiction Aquatic Development — a fish market, sashimi bar, and standing oyster bar all in one. Then head to Taoyuan Airport.
Arrive in Jaipur and head straight to Amber Fort — ride up the hillside, explore mirror-inlaid chambers, and gaze down at Maota Lake.
Visit Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds) and the City Palace, then wander the pink-painted bazaars of Johari Bazaar for gemstones and textiles.
Dinner at Tapri Central, a rooftop cafe overlooking the Nahargarh Fort with excellent chai and Rajasthani thali.
Explore Jantar Mantar, the 18th-century astronomical observatory with giant sundials, then shop for block-printed textiles at Anokhi.
Drive 5 hours to Jodhpur (or take the train). Watch the blue-painted houses appear as you approach the Blue City.
Dinner on a rooftop with Mehrangarh Fort lit up above you — Indique or Stepwell Cafe both have stunning fort views and great laal maas (spicy lamb).
Explore Mehrangarh Fort — one of India's most impressive fortresses, rising 400 feet above the city. The audio guide (narrated by a local historian) is excellent.
Walk the blue-painted lanes of the old city below the fort, stopping at spice shops and the clock tower market for lassi at Mishrilal Hotel (since 1927).
Watch sunset from Pachetia Hill for the most photogenic view of the blue city, then eat mirchi bada (chili fritters) and kachori at local street stalls.
Drive toward Udaipur, stopping at Ranakpur Jain Temple — 1,444 intricately carved marble pillars, no two alike. It's one of India's most astonishing buildings.
Arrive in Udaipur and take a boat ride on Lake Pichola. See the Lake Palace hotel floating on the water and the City Palace rising above the ghats.
Dinner at Ambrai Restaurant on the lake shore with candlelit views of the Lake Palace and Jag Mandir. Order the paneer tikka and dal baati churma.
Tour the massive City Palace complex, then walk through the old town's narrow lanes past havelis (ornate townhouses) and craft workshops.
Visit Saheliyon Ki Bari (Garden of the Maidens) and the Vintage Car Museum, then browse miniature paintings in the art galleries along Gangaur Ghat.
Catch a Dharohar folk dance show at Bagore Ki Haveli, then farewell dinner at Upre with a panoramic rooftop view of the lit-up palace.
Fly into Kochi and head to Fort Kochi. Walk past the iconic Chinese fishing nets along the waterfront — they've been here since the 14th century.
Explore the Mattancherry Palace, the Jewish Synagogue on Jew Town Road, and the colorful spice shops selling fresh cardamom and pepper.
Watch a Kathakali dance performance at Kerala Kathakali Centre, then eat fresh fish curry and appam at Fort House Hotel restaurant on the harbor.
Drive 2 hours to Alleppey (Alappuzha) and board a traditional kettuvallam houseboat. Glide through palm-fringed canals as the crew cooks lunch.
Float past rice paddies, toddy shops, and village life along the backwater channels. Stop at a coir (coconut fiber) workshop to see rope-making.
Your houseboat anchors in a quiet spot. Eat a Kerala feast of fish moilee, avial, and rice cooked onboard, watching fireflies over the water.
Drive 4 hours into the Western Ghats to Munnar. The road climbs through waterfalls and spice plantations as the air turns cool.
Tour the Tata Tea Museum to learn about Munnar's colonial tea history, then walk through the rolling tea estates with a local guide.
Settle into a hillside homestay. Eat a home-cooked Kerala dinner of puttu, kadala curry, and banana chips while mist rolls over the valleys.
Drive to Eravikulam National Park for a chance to spot Nilgiri tahr (endangered mountain goats) among the shola grasslands.
Hike to Top Station for panoramic views into Tamil Nadu, then visit a cardamom plantation to smell, taste, and buy the freshest spices.
Ayurvedic massage at a local spa — Kerala is the birthplace of Ayurveda, and even basic treatments here are the real deal.
Drive down to Marari Beach near Alleppey — a quiet fishing village beach with golden sand and swaying palms, far from tourist crowds.
Swim, watch fishermen haul in their catch, and eat a final Kerala fish fry at a beachside shack with fresh toddy (palm wine).
Transfer to Kochi airport. Pick up Malabar coffee and banana chips as farewell gifts from the spice coast.
Visit Boudhanath Stupa — one of the largest in the world. Walk clockwise spinning prayer wheels with Tibetan monks as chanting echoes around the dome.
Head to Pashupatinath Temple on the Bagmati River — observe Hindu cremation ceremonies (at a respectful distance) at this sacred site.
Dinner in Thamel at OR2K, a vegetarian Middle Eastern restaurant that's a traveler institution, then explore the buzzing backpacker district.
Explore Kathmandu Durbar Square — carved wooden temples, the living goddess Kumari's palace, and the old royal palace buildings.
Drive to Patan Durbar Square (30 minutes) — many say it's even more impressive. The Patan Museum inside the old palace is Nepal's finest.
Eat dal bhat (the Nepali national meal of lentils and rice) at Bhojan Griha, a restored Newari merchant house with traditional dancing.
Drive to Nagarkot for sunrise over the Himalayan range — on a clear day you can see Everest, Langtang, and Ganesh Himal in one sweeping panorama.
Hike down (3 hours) to Bhaktapur, the best-preserved medieval city in the valley. Its pottery square and 55-window palace are photogenic treasures.
Try juju dhau (king of yogurt) in Bhaktapur — a creamy buffalo-milk yogurt served in clay pots. Have momo dumplings at a local shop before heading back.
Climb the 365 steps to Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple) for a hilltop stupa surrounded by cheeky monkeys and prayer flags with city views.
Take a half-day hike around the Shivapuri Nagarjun National Park — lush rhododendron forests just 30 minutes from the city center.
Explore Lazimpat's restaurant row — try Nepali craft beer at Himalayan Java and Newari cuisine at Newa Lahana in a traditional courtyard.
Book a 1-hour Everest mountain flight — you'll fly along the Himalayan range and see Everest from your window seat. Worth every penny.
Last shopping in Thamel for pashmina scarves, singing bowls, and thangka paintings. Bargain respectfully — start at half the asking price.
Farewell momo feast at Yangling Restaurant (Thamel's most famous momo spot since the 1970s), then transfer to Tribhuvan International Airport.
Explore Colombo's Pettah Market for spices and textiles, then visit Gangaramaya Temple — an eclectic Buddhist temple with an incredible museum.
Take the scenic train to Kandy (3 hours) through lush hills and tea country. Book a second-class window seat for the best views.
Walk around Kandy Lake at dusk, then eat rice and curry at The White House Restaurant — a local favorite with over 15 curries on one plate.

days.title: Kandy & the Temple of the Tooth

activities.description: Visit the Temple of the Tooth Relic (Sri Dalada Maligawa) — Sri Lanka's most sacred Buddhist site, housing a tooth of the Buddha.
Tour the Royal Botanical Gardens at Peradeniya — 150 acres of orchids, giant fig trees, and a bat colony of thousands.
Attend a Kandyan dance performance (drums, fire walking, acrobatics), then drive to Ella through tea plantation country.
Hike Little Adam's Peak at sunrise — an easy 45-minute walk rewarded with 360-degree views of tea-covered mountains and valleys.
Walk to the Nine Arches Bridge (Demodara) and wait for a train to cross — the brick bridge framed by jungle is Sri Lanka's most photographed spot.
Cook Sri Lankan food with a local family in Ella, learning to make dhal curry, pol sambol, and hoppers from scratch.
Drive to Sigiriya and climb the ancient rock fortress — 1,200 steps past frescoes and lion paw gates to a palace complex on the summit.
Visit the lesser-known Pidurangala Rock next door for a stunning view LOOKING BACK at Sigiriya — far fewer tourists and an equally epic climb.
Drive to Mirissa on the south coast (5 hours). Settle into a beach guesthouse and eat fresh grilled fish at Dewmini Roti Shop.
Join an early morning whale watching boat from Mirissa harbor — blue whales and spinner dolphins are regularly spotted from December to April.
Relax on Mirissa Beach, surf the point break, and visit the stilt fishermen at Koggala (best at dawn, but photo-worthy anytime).
Last sunset and seafood dinner on the beach before transferring to Bandaranaike International Airport near Colombo.
Arrive by seaplane or speedboat to your resort atoll. Check into your overwater villa and jump straight off the deck into the turquoise lagoon.
Snorkel the house reef directly below your villa — reef sharks, sea turtles, and thousands of tropical fish without going anywhere.
Sunset dinner on the beach or overwater deck — fresh tuna sashimi and lobster while the sky turns pink over the Indian Ocean.
Join a guided snorkeling trip to a nearby reef for manta ray cleaning stations — watch these gentle giants glide meters from you.
Try a discover scuba dive (no certification needed) on the house reef, or go deep-sea fishing with a local captain.
Book the resort's underwater restaurant or sandbank dinner — dining on a private island with your feet in the sand.
Kayak or paddleboard around the island at sunrise. The water is so clear you can see stingrays gliding below your board.
Take a sunset dolphin cruise — pods of spinner dolphins leap alongside the dhoni (traditional boat) nearly every evening.
Couples spa treatment over the water with ocean sounds below, followed by a private beach dinner arranged by the resort.
Visit a nearby local island to see real Maldivian life — the mosque, the school, and fishermen bringing in the morning catch.
Last swim from your villa deck, one more snorkel on the house reef, and a fresh coconut from the island's palm trees.
Transfer by speedboat or seaplane to Male airport. Pick up Maldivian lacquerware or coconut oil products at the airport shops.
Start with croissants at Du Pain et des Idees in the 10th, then walk along the Seine's Left Bank past the bouquinistes (book stalls).
Explore the Musee d'Orsay — the Impressionist collection in a converted train station. Don't miss the Renoir and Monet rooms on the top floor.
Picnic under the Eiffel Tower at Champ de Mars with wine, cheese, and baguette from a nearby fromagerie. Watch the tower sparkle at the top of each hour.
Enter the Louvre at opening (9 AM, book timed tickets). See the Mona Lisa first, then explore the Egyptian antiquities and Winged Victory.
Walk through the Tuileries Garden to Place des Vosges in Le Marais. Browse vintage shops and falafel joints on Rue des Rosiers.
Dinner at Le Bouillon Chartier — a stunning Belle Epoque dining room serving classic French dishes at impossibly low prices since 1896.
Climb to Sacre-Coeur Basilica and watch the city wake up from the steps. Walk through Place du Tertre where artists still paint portraits.
Explore Montmartre's quieter streets — Cafe des Deux Moulins (from Amelie), the Montmartre vineyard, and Le Mur des Je T'aime (Wall of Love).
Dinner at Pink Mamma in the 10th — a 4-story Italian restaurant with a secret rooftop terrace and incredible truffle pasta.
Train to Versailles (40 minutes). Enter through the back gardens first to beat crowds, then work your way into the Hall of Mirrors.
Rent a rowboat on the Grand Canal, then explore Marie Antoinette's Hamlet — a fairy-tale fake village she built to escape court life.
Back in Paris, walk the illuminated Pont Alexandre III bridge, then dinner at Breizh Cafe for the best buckwheat galettes and hard cider.
Visit the Sainte-Chapelle — 15 massive stained glass windows from 1248 that will take your breath away. Go when morning sun lights them up.
Explore Canal Saint-Martin's iron footbridges and indie shops, then grab ice cream at Berthillon on Ile Saint-Louis.
Farewell dinner at Le Comptoir du Pantheon in the Latin Quarter, then walk along the Seine one final time as the city glows.
Enter the Colosseum at opening (book skip-the-line tickets). Walk the arena floor where gladiators fought, then head to the Roman Forum.
Climb Palatine Hill for views over the Forum ruins and the Circus Maximus. Rest at a cafe near the Capitoline Museums.
Dinner in Trastevere at Da Enzo al 29 — order the cacio e pepe and the fried artichokes (carciofi alla giudia). Expect a wait but it's worth it.
Book an early-entry Vatican Museums tour (7:30 AM). Walk through the Gallery of Maps and Raphael Rooms before crowds, ending at the Sistine Chapel ceiling.
Step into St. Peter's Basilica (free entry) and climb the dome for a bird's-eye view of St. Peter's Square. See Michelangelo's Pieta near the entrance.
Walk to Prati neighborhood for dinner at Pizzarium — Rome's best pizza al taglio (by the slice), run by pizza legend Gabriele Bonci.
Start at the Trevi Fountain (go before 8 AM for a crowd-free experience), then walk to the Spanish Steps and the Piazza di Spagna.
Explore the Pantheon — free entry to the best-preserved Roman building, with its 2,000-year-old concrete dome open to the sky.
Aperitivo at Salotto 42 near the Pantheon, then dinner at Roscioli for their legendary carbonara and hand-selected wine list.
Visit the Borghese Gallery (reservation required) — Bernini's sculptures of Apollo and Daphne and David will give you chills.
Walk through the Villa Borghese gardens to Piazza del Popolo, then explore the Testaccio neighborhood — Rome's original foodie quarter.
Eat at Flavio al Velavevodetto in Testaccio, built into an ancient Roman trash heap (Monte Testaccio). The amatriciana is the city's best.
Rent a bike and ride the ancient Appian Way — a 2,300-year-old Roman road lined with ruins, catacombs, and umbrella pines.
Visit the catacombs of San Callisto underground, then head back to the centro storico for last shopping around Campo de' Fiori.
Farewell gelato at Fatamorgana (try the Kentucky — tobacco and walnut), a final espresso at a bar, then arrivederci Roma.
Wander the narrow medieval lanes of the Barri Gotic — visit the Cathedral of Barcelona and stumble upon hidden plazas like Placa de Sant Felip Neri.
Walk La Rambla (briefly — it's touristy) then duck into La Boqueria Market for fresh juices, jamon iberico, and seafood cups from Pinotxo Bar.
Tapas crawl through El Born — start at Bar del Pla for patatas bravas, then Cal Pep for fried fish, and finish at La Vinya del Senyor for cava by the glass.
Visit the Sagrada Familia at opening (book the Nativity tower ticket). Gaudi's unfinished masterpiece will permanently change how you see architecture.
Walk up Passeig de Gracia to see Casa Batllo and Casa Mila (La Pedrera) — Gaudi's fantastical apartment buildings with rooftop warrior chimneys.
Dinner at Cerveceria Catalana — one of Barcelona's best tapas bars. Order the mini hamburgers, grilled prawns, and Galician-style octopus.
Enter Park Guell at 8 AM (timed ticket required) for Gaudi's mosaic wonderland with views across Barcelona to the sea. Walk the trails above for free.
Explore the Gracia neighborhood — bohemian plazas, vintage shops, and locals sipping vermouth. Grab lunch at La Pepita for inventive montaditos.
Watch sunset from Bunkers del Carmel — a civil war bunker turned into Barcelona's best (and free) sunset viewpoint. Bring a bottle of wine.
Swim and walk along Barceloneta Beach. Rent a paddleboard or just people-watch from a chiringuito (beach bar).
Long lunch at Can Paixano (La Xampanyeria) in Barceloneta — cheap cava and bocadillos standing elbow-to-elbow with locals. Then visit the Picasso Museum.
Splurge on paella at Can Ros, a family-run seafood restaurant in Barceloneta since 1911. Order the arroz negro (black squid ink rice).
Take the cable car up Montjuic hill. Visit the Joan Miro Foundation for playful modern art, then explore the hilltop castle and gardens.
Walk through the Raval neighborhood for street art and a visit to MACBA (the contemporary art museum with its famous skatepark plaza).
Farewell vermouth and olives at a plaza in Sant Antoni, then one last plate of pa amb tomaquet before heading to El Prat airport.
Watch the Changing of the Guard at Buckingham Palace (check schedule — not daily in winter), then walk through St. James's Park.
Visit the Tower of London to see the Crown Jewels and hear Beefeater stories, then cross Tower Bridge for the best Thames views.
Dinner at Dishoom Shoreditch — London's beloved Bombay-style cafe. The black daal and lamb biryani are non-negotiable.
The British Museum is free and mind-blowing. See the Rosetta Stone, Parthenon Marbles, and Egyptian mummies in a couple of focused hours.
Walk the South Bank from the Tate Modern (free!) past Shakespeare's Globe to Borough Market — London's best food market since 1756.
Catch a show in the West End (book same-day TKTS at Leicester Square for discounts), then late-night fish and chips at The Golden Hind in Marylebone.
Explore Portobello Road Market in Notting Hill (best on Saturdays) — antiques, vintage clothing, and street food in pastel-colored streets.
Walk through Hyde Park and Kensington Gardens to the Victoria and Albert Museum — the world's greatest museum of design and decorative arts (free).
Pub crawl through Soho — start at The French House (De Gaulle's wartime haunt), then The Dog and Duck, ending at a Chinatown dumpling spot.
Explore Shoreditch's street art — Brick Lane, Fashion Street, and Rivington Street. Pop into Beigel Bake for a salt beef bagel (open 24 hours since 1974).
Browse the Columbia Road Flower Market (Sundays only) or Spitalfields Market (daily), then visit the Dennis Severs' House — a time-capsule of 18th-century London.
Dinner at St. John Smithfield for nose-to-tail British cooking — the bone marrow and parsley salad is legendary. Book ahead.
Take the Thames Clipper boat to Greenwich. Stand on the Prime Meridian line at the Royal Observatory and set your watch to GMT.
Explore the Cutty Sark tea clipper and Greenwich Market, then walk through Greenwich Park for a panoramic view of Canary Wharf's skyline.
Back in central London, farewell afternoon tea at Sketch (the pink room is iconic), then one last pint at a proper local pub before Heathrow.
Rent a bike (this is how Amsterdam moves) and ride the Herengracht and Prinsengracht canals, stopping at the Nine Streets for indie boutiques.
Visit the Rijksmuseum — Rembrandt's Night Watch, Vermeer's Milkmaid, and the Delft pottery collection. The building itself is a masterpiece.
Dinner at De Foodhallen in Oud-West — a food hall in a former tram depot with everything from Vietnamese bao to Dutch bitterballen.
Visit the Anne Frank House (book 6 weeks ahead online — tickets release at 10 AM). The hidden annex behind the bookcase is unforgettable.
Explore the Jordaan neighborhood — browse the Noordermarkt (Saturdays) for organic food, walk along Bloemgracht, and visit local galleries.
Indonesian rijsttafel (rice table — 12+ dishes) at Blauw or Tempo Doeloe. It's Amsterdam's signature dining experience from its colonial history.
The Van Gogh Museum has the world's largest collection — follow his artistic journey from dark Dutch paintings to blazing Sunflowers. Book a morning slot.
Relax in Vondelpark with an Albert Heijn picnic and a local beer, or rent a pedal boat on the canals for a water-level view of the city.
Bar hop along Leidseplein and Rembrandtplein. Try a brown cafe (traditional Dutch pub) like Cafe 't Smalle in Jordaan for a jenever tasting.
Free ferry to NDSM Wharf — a post-industrial art district with warehouses turned into studios, a monthly flea market, and great street art.
Visit the Heineken Experience for an interactive brewery tour, or the FOAM photography museum for something more curated.
Farewell herring from a haringhandel (herring cart), apple pie at Cafe Winkel 43, and a last canal-side walk before Schiphol.
Arrive by ferry or flight and settle into a cave hotel in Oia or Fira. The caldera views from your terrace are worth every euro.
Wander Oia's narrow lanes of whitewashed houses, blue domes, and bougainvillea. Visit the Maritime Museum and browse the art galleries.
Stake out a spot near the Oia Castle ruins for what's considered one of the world's best sunsets. Dinner at Ammoudi Bay — climb 300 steps down for grilled octopus by the water.
Visit Red Beach (short walk from Akrotiri) — dramatic red volcanic cliffs meeting dark sand and crystal water. Go early before it gets packed.
Wine tasting at Santo Wines or Venetsanos Winery — both have tasting rooms overlooking the caldera. Try the dry Assyrtiko, the island's signature grape.
Dinner in Fira at Argo restaurant with balcony seating over the caldera. The lamb kleftiko and fava bean puree are standouts.
Boat trip to the volcanic island of Nea Kameni — hike to the steaming crater rim and look down into the caldera that created Santorini.
Swim in the hot springs at Palea Kameni (the water is warm and sulfurous — don't wear white), then sail back past Thirassia island.
Hike the caldera trail from Fira to Oia (10 km, 3 hours) in the late afternoon for spectacular views, arriving in Oia just in time for sunset.
Visit Akrotiri archaeological site — a Minoan city buried by a volcanic eruption in 1600 BC, remarkably preserved like a Greek Pompeii.
Relax at Perissa Black Beach — rent a sunbed, swim in the warm Aegean, and eat gyros at a beachfront taverna.
Last glass of Vinsanto (sweet wine made from sun-dried grapes) at a cliffside bar, then transfer to the airport or ferry port.
Walk across Charles Bridge at dawn (by 7 AM) when it's nearly empty and the morning mist rises off the Vltava. The 30 baroque statues glow in the light.
Explore Old Town Square — watch the Astronomical Clock strike the hour, visit the Church of Our Lady before Tyn, and get trdelnik from a street vendor.
Dinner at Lokal Dlouhaaa for authentic Czech food — svickova (beef sirloin in cream sauce) with knedliky (dumplings) and a tank of Pilsner Urquell.
Climb to Prague Castle (the world's largest ancient castle complex). Walk through St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and Golden Lane's tiny colorful houses.
Descend through the Mala Strana (Lesser Town) — baroque palaces, hidden gardens, and the John Lennon Wall covered in peace graffiti since the 1980s.
Beer tasting at Strahov Monastery Brewery — monks have brewed here since the 13th century. Pair the St. Norbert amber with smoked meats.
Tour the Jewish Museum and Old Jewish Cemetery (12,000 headstones stacked in layers). The Spanish Synagogue's ornate Moorish interior is breathtaking.
Explore Vinohrady and Zizkov neighborhoods — Prague's hipster heart. Climb the Zizkov TV Tower for panoramic views and spot the crawling baby sculptures.
Pub crawl Prague-style: start at U Zlateho Tygra (The Golden Tiger, Vaclav Havel's favorite pub), then hit the underground bars in Zizkov.
Visit Vysehrad fortress — a clifftop citadel with sweeping river views, fewer tourists than the castle, and a cemetery where Dvorak and Mucha are buried.
Stroll along the Naplavka riverbank market (weekends), then visit DOX Centre for Contemporary Art or the Museum of Communism.
Farewell dinner at Kantyna for the best butcher-to-table steak in Prague, then one last Czech beer (they drink more per capita than anywhere on earth).
Walk the complete 2-kilometer City Walls circuit — start at the Pile Gate entrance early (8 AM) before the cruise ship crowds arrive.
Cool off at Buza Bar — a hidden cliff bar carved into the outer wall. Order a cold Ozujsko beer and jump off the rocks into the Adriatic.
Dinner at Proto Fish Restaurant on Siroka Street for fresh Adriatic catch, or Pantarul in the neighborhood outside the walls for modern Croatian cooking.
Take the 15-minute ferry to Lokrum Island — a car-free nature reserve with a monastery ruin, botanical garden, and the Iron Throne from Game of Thrones.
Swim in the Dead Sea — a saltwater lake in the middle of the island that's warm and impossibly buoyant. Snorkel the rocky coves.
Back in the Old Town, walk the Stradun (main street) at sunset when the marble glows, then eat at Barba for street-food-style seafood.
Ride the Dubrovnik Cable Car to Mount Srd for a jaw-dropping panorama of the walled city, Lokrum Island, and the Adriatic coastline stretching south.
Join a sea kayaking tour around the city walls — paddle under the fortresses and into Betina Cave, then swim at a secluded beach.
Sunset drinks at 360 by Jeffrey's (a rooftop bar on the city walls), then dinner at Konoba Jezuite up the steep stairs — their risotto is incredible.
Take a boat tour to the Elaphiti Islands — Lopud, Sipan, and Kolocep. Start at Lopud's Sunj Beach, the only sandy beach in the Dubrovnik area.
Explore Sipan Island's olive groves and medieval captain's houses, sample local wine and fresh oysters from Ston.
Last walk through the Old Town at dusk when most tourists have left, farewell seafood at Taj Mahal (Bosnian, despite the name — the cevapi are amazing).
Explore colorful downtown Reykjavik — Hallgrimskirkja church tower for city views, Harpa Concert Hall's glass facade, and the Sun Voyager sculpture.
Drive 45 minutes to the Blue Lagoon. Soak in the milky blue geothermal water with a silica mud mask and a drink from the in-water bar.
Dinner at Grillid for modern Icelandic tasting menus, or Baejarins Beztu for a famous Icelandic hot dog (mustard, remoulade, crunchy onions).
Drive the Golden Circle — first stop: Thingvellir National Park, where you can walk between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates.
Watch Geysir's Strokkur geyser erupt every 5-10 minutes, then stand at the edge of Gullfoss waterfall as glacial water plunges into a canyon.
Soak in the Secret Lagoon in Fludir (less crowded and cheaper than Blue Lagoon), then drive back for lamb soup at Svarta Kaffid in Reykjavik.
Drive the South Coast to Seljalandsfoss waterfall — you can walk behind the curtain of water. Then visit nearby Skogafoss and climb the stairs to the top.
Continue to Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach — dramatic basalt columns, crashing waves, and sea stacks. Stay back from the sneaker waves, they're genuinely dangerous.
Visit the Vik area and drive back, stopping for dinner at Smidjan Brugghus in Reykjavik for craft beers and slow-smoked Arctic char.
Join a glacier hiking tour on Solheimajokull — strap on crampons and walk across blue ice crevasses with a certified guide. No experience needed.
If time allows, drive to Jokulsarlon glacier lagoon to see massive icebergs floating in a lake, and Diamond Beach where ice chunks wash ashore.
In winter (Sep-Mar), hunt for the Northern Lights away from city lights — many tours drive to the best viewing spots based on the aurora forecast.
Snorkel Silfra Fissure in Thingvellir — crystal-clear glacial water between two continental plates with 100-meter visibility. You'll wear a drysuit.
Drive the Reykjanes Peninsula past steaming lava fields and the Bridge Between Continents. Visit the Reykjanes Lighthouse area.
Last meal of Icelandic lamb at Dill (Iceland's only Michelin-starred restaurant — book months ahead) or Messinn for a skillet of fresh fish stew.
Ride the iconic Tram 28 through Alfama's narrow streets (board at Martim Moniz to get a seat), then walk back down through the oldest neighborhood in Lisbon.
Visit the Sao Jorge Castle for panoramic city views, then wind through Alfama's labyrinth of alleyways, azulejo-tiled facades, and hidden courtyards.
Dinner at a fado house in Alfama — Tasca do Chico or Mesa de Frades for raw, emotional Portuguese guitar music over petiscos (small plates).
Take the tram to Belem. Visit the Jeronimos Monastery (stunning Manueline architecture) and the Tower of Belem on the Tagus waterfront.
Eat pasteis de nata at Pasteis de Belem (the original since 1837 — dust with cinnamon), then visit the MAAT contemporary art museum.
Cross to the south bank for dinner at Ponto Final in Cacilhas — cheap, incredible seafood with a view back across the river to Lisbon's skyline.
Ride the Santa Justa Elevator for city views, then walk through the Baixa grid to the pink-hued Praca do Comercio on the waterfront.
Lunch at Time Out Market — Lisbon's best chefs under one roof. Try Cevicheria's Peruvian-Portuguese fusion or Manteigaria for warm custard tarts.
Walk up to Miradouro da Graca for sunset views, then bar-hop through Bairro Alto — the entire hillside neighborhood turns into a street party after 10 PM.
Train to Sintra (40 minutes). Start at the psychedelic Pena Palace — a hilltop fairy-tale castle painted in yellow, red, and purple.
Explore the Quinta da Regaleira — mysterious underground tunnels, initiatic wells you spiral down into, and gardens out of a fantasy novel.
Back in Lisbon, farewell ginjinha (sour cherry liqueur) at A Ginjinha near Rossio, then sunset sardines at Cervejaria Ramiro — the best shellfish restaurant in the city.
Train into Interlaken Ost, nestled between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz. Check into a guesthouse with mountain views and get your bearings.
Take a boat cruise on Lake Brienz — turquoise glacial water surrounded by waterfalls and steep Alpine meadows. Stop at Giessbach Falls.
Dinner at Restaurant Baren for Swiss classics — raclette, rosti, and a local beer. Walk along the Aare River as the mountains glow pink at sunset.
Take the cogwheel train to Jungfraujoch (3,454m) — the highest train station in Europe. Views of the Aletsch Glacier are otherworldly.
Walk through the Ice Palace carved inside the glacier, step onto the Sphinx observation deck, and (weather permitting) hike the snow trail.
Descend to Grindelwald village for cheese fondue at Hotel Gletschergarten — melted Gruyere with bread, pickles, and kirsch.
Train to Lauterbrunnen — a valley with 72 waterfalls. Walk to Staubbach Falls, which plunges 300 meters right next to the village.
Take the cable car to Murren, a car-free village perched on a cliff. Hike the Northface Trail with views of Eiger, Monch, and Jungfrau.
Dinner at Hotel Eiger in Murren with a window seat facing the Eiger's infamous north face. Try the Zurcher Geschnetzeltes (Zurich-style veal).
Scenic train ride to Zermatt (about 3 hours with changes) through the Lotschberg tunnel and Rhone Valley — every window is a postcard.
Arrive in car-free Zermatt. Walk through the village and find your first view of the Matterhorn — Switzerland's most iconic mountain.
Dinner at Chez Vrony, a mountain restaurant above Zermatt with Matterhorn views and the best lamb in the valley. Book ahead.
Take the Gornergrat cogwheel railway to 3,089 meters. The 360-degree panorama of 29 peaks over 4,000 meters (including Monte Rosa) is staggering.
Hike down from Gornergrat to Riffelsee lake — on a still day the Matterhorn reflects perfectly in the water. Classic Swiss postcard moment.
Last Swiss chocolate and espresso in Zermatt's Bahnhofstrasse, then train to Geneva or Zurich airport through more impossibly beautiful scenery.
Enter the Hagia Sophia at opening — 1,500 years old, once a church, then a mosque, now a mosque again. The massive dome and golden mosaics are awe-inspiring.
Walk across to the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) — six minarets and 20,000 blue Iznik tiles. Visit between prayer times and cover shoulders and knees.
Dinner at Sultanahmet Koftecisi (since 1920) for the city's best kofte (grilled meatballs), then walk through the illuminated Hippodrome.
Lose yourself in the Grand Bazaar — 4,000+ shops across 60 streets. Focus on the old bedesten (original covered market) for leather, ceramics, and kilim rugs.
Walk downhill to the Spice Bazaar (Egyptian Bazaar) for Turkish delight, dried fruits, and saffron. Pop into Rustem Pasha Mosque hidden above the market.
Cross the Galata Bridge at sunset watching fishermen, then climb the medieval Galata Tower for 360-degree views of the city straddling two continents.
Take the public ferry Bosphorus cruise from Eminonu — 90 minutes past palaces, wooden mansions, and the Rumeli Fortress. A fraction of the price of private tours.
Disembark in Kadikoy on the Asian side. Explore the Moda neighborhood, the fish market, and the trendy cafes of Baris Manco Street.
Eat at Ciya Sofrasi in Kadikoy — Chef Musa Dagdeviren serves forgotten Anatolian recipes. Try the kebab from southeastern Turkey and the quince dessert.
Tour Topkapi Palace — the Ottoman sultans' home for 400 years. The Harem rooms, treasury (86-carat diamond), and Bosphorus views are extraordinary.
Experience a traditional Turkish hammam at Kilic Ali Pasa Hamami (beautifully restored) or the historic Cagaloglu Hamami — scrub, steam, and soap massage.
Walk through the hip Karakoy neighborhood, then dinner at Mikla on a rooftop — Turkish-Scandinavian fusion with a view of the Golden Horn.
Visit the Basilica Cistern — a subterranean palace of 336 marble columns with atmospheric lighting and the upside-down Medusa heads.
Explore Istiklal Caddesi and the Beyoglu district — once the European quarter, now full of record shops, pastry houses, and the nostalgic red tram.
Farewell Turkish breakfast spread (simit, olives, cheese, honey, eggs, sucuk sausage) at Van Kahvalti Evi, then transfer to Istanbul Airport.
